caption:
Google's Gemini app is now rolling out on Apple CarPlay, so iPhone users can talk to Gemini Live hands-free from the car's display.
It can read your daily brief, sum up unread email and pick up a chat you started on your phone.
Gemini was the last big chatbot missing from CarPlay.

Would you let an AI read your inbox while you drive?

paragraphs.text: Google began rolling out a dedicated Gemini app for Apple CarPlay on November 11, 2026, letting iPhone users hold hands-free voice conversations with Gemini Live from their car's display, according to 9to5Google and Engadget. The rollout started worldwide for iOS users in every language that Gemini Live supports.

Before this release, some Gemini features were available on CarPlay only inside Google Maps. The new app brings the full Gemini Live conversation experience to the dashboard as its own icon, MacRumors and Engadget reported. Google already offers Gemini on Android Auto and Android Automotive.
What Gemini can do in the car

The CarPlay interface is deliberately simple. It shows a waveform that indicates when Gemini is listening, thinking or responding, with End and Mute buttons in the top left corner, according to 9to5Google. As on the phone, drivers can interrupt Gemini Live mid-answer to add a detail, change the subject or pause the conversation.

Google's suggested uses include checking the day's calendar, hearing a daily brief, summarizing Gmail threads, finding places nearby and rehearsing a presentation on the drive. Digital Trends reported that, through Gmail and Calendar, Gemini can read out a daily brief, summarize unread email and help draft spoken replies. MacRumors gave the example of asking for a quick lunch spot in downtown Austin that is easy to get in and out of.

Conversations started in the car sync with the Gemini app on the iPhone and stay in the chat history, and drivers can resume a recent chat or start a new one. Google described the CarPlay version as designed to work like a conversational driving companion that minimizes distraction, according to 9to5Google.

Engadget and Digital Trends list three requirements: the latest version of the Gemini app on the iPhone, microphone permission turned on, and at least one earlier use of Gemini Live on the phone. After that, drivers tap the Gemini icon on the CarPlay screen. Digital Trends also noted that the Daily Brief feature has to be switched on before it can be used in the car.

CarPlay began supporting voice-based conversational AI apps with iOS 26.4, MacRumors reported. ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Copilot, Perplexity and Meta AI were already available on CarPlay, which made Gemini the last major chatbot to arrive, according to MacRumors and Digital Trends.

The car is becoming another place where AI assistants compete for daily use. Gemini's main advantage there is its link to Gmail and Google Calendar, which lets it turn a commute into time for catching up on email and the day's schedule without touching the phone.
Watch whether Google brings its Personal Intelligence features, which it is adding to Gemini on Android Auto and in cars with Google built-in, to the CarPlay app as well.
